messages:
maria: quick heads-up — our raven-lite canary is spiking parse failures for streaming funcalls, ~3.2% on last hour. looks like models are interjecting short natural-language lines between NDJSON objects (e.g. 'note:' / 'thinking...')
ravi: can you paste a minimal example of what you're seeing?
maria: yup. here's a real chunk from the capture (streaming):
```
{"tool":"search","args":{"q":"redwood latency"}}
note: expanding terms to include 'p99'
{"tool":"filter","args":{"k":"region","v":"us-west-2"}}
```
maria: parser chokes because those lines aren't valid JSON; our stream-ndjson reader assumes each line is JSON.
aj: this is kinda new — we've seen truncated tokens before, but free-text interjections are surprising. any idea why model emits these? prompt/template changes?
maria: not local to prompts; seen across a few canaries and different prompts. seems quantized variant more likely but not exclusive.
sam: emoji :eyes: — if it's reproducible, we should avoid blanket regex hacks that silently drop content. that could mask model hallucination vs intended commentary.
ravi: Agreed. proposal: add a "strip_interjections" postprocess that (a) detects lines that are not JSON, (b) attempts light repair, (c) if repair succeeds use repaired stream, else send raw payload to mirror subsystem for offline analysis. we should also emit a histogram of interjection token positions.
aj: for (b) what heuristics do you have in mind? simple rules first: drop blank lines, drop lines matching ^(note|thinking|edit):, and try to merge adjacent fragments until we can parse a JSON object. example pseudo: 
```python
lines = stream.splitlines()
for i,line in enumerate(lines):
  if line.strip().startswith('{'): try: json.loads(line); continue
  if re.match(r'^(note|thinking|edit)[:\- ]', line.strip(), re.I): drop line
  else: try merge with next lines up to 3 lines and json.loads(merged)
```
aj: keep it bounded to avoid weird concatenations.
sam: add telemetry: emit repair_action = {dropped,line_merged,failed_repair} with the original snippet id. we should also log the full original to S3 for short TTL (30d) for triage.
maria: I like that. also want an eval to check for semantic regressions: before/after stripping run the structured-output conformance test suite (the golden prompt set) and check funcall success/field-level fidelity. we might accidentally remove a legitimate explanatory field (e.g., "notes": "...") that downstream relies on.
ravi: good call. test design idea: A/B traffic in canary — 50% raw, 50% stripped_interjections. capture parse_fail_rate, funcall_success_rate, and downstream JSON-schema rejection rate. run at least 5k samples per arm.
aj: operationally we'll gate the feature behind rollout flags: `enable_strip_interjections` + `enable_stream_mirror`. default false.
canary-bot: deploy scheduled: canary: raven-lite-quantized v2 -> routing split 50/50 at 2025-11-07T17:40Z (job id cny-8321).
maria: assigning tasks: 
- aj: prototype heuristics + unit tests + feature flag (ETA: tomorrow morning)
- sam: add telemetry schema + S3 sink + alert if repair_rate > 1% of requests (ETA: EOD)
- ravi: design eval harness for semantic/regression A/B (ETA: 48h)
- maria: run initial sampling and annotate ~200 failures for root-cause (ETA: today)
sam: add automation to fail the canary if stripped arm shows >0.5% drop in funcall_success vs raw. safety net.
aj: noted. I'll avoid destructive merges and will keep the original stream in the mirror.
ravi: one more thought — if we detect frequent inline narration tokens, we could also add a lightweight prompt-safety signal (token-level cost) to nudge model away in oncalls, but that's longer-term.
maria: for immediate next step I'll drop a small dataset of examples into #eng-ml and link here. thanks all — will update when canary posts metrics. :thumbsup:
canary-bot: canary metrics posted: parse_fail_rate(raw)=3.21%, parse_fail_rate(stripped)=0.87%, repair_actions=dropped:1.9%, merged:0.4%, failed_repair:0.1% (first 2k reqs).
sam: preliminary looks promising but need semantic checks (ravi). :mag_right:
ravi: I'll start evals now and report back with schema field diffs and any significant deltas.
maria: great, keeping this thread for triage notes and link to sample corpus once uploaded.
